title: HPIM-NoC: A Priori-Knowledge-Based Optimization Framework for Heterogeneous PIM-Based NoCs
problem: Existing NoC simulators and architecture search frameworks are designed for homogeneous architectures and lack support for simulating and optimizing heterogeneous Processing-in-Memory (PIM) configurations with varied core capabilities.
motivation: Heterogeneous PIM-based NoC accelerators achieve superior performance than homogeneous designs for neural networks, but current search frameworks only explore workload allocation and mapping, missing the larger design space of heterogeneous PIM configurations.
method: HPIM-NoC combines simulation and search to optimize systems where different types of processing cores are connected by a network-on-chip (a grid of communication channels on the chip). It accurately models how long data takes to travel through the network by simulating transmission delays. The system searches for good designs in three stages using a customized simulated annealing algorithm (a method that gradually refines solutions by testing variations), guided by prior knowledge about architecture. To accelerate the search, it pre-calculates performance metrics for each core type, reduces simulation frequency for the network, and applies a customized layout algorithm.
key_novelty: The framework enables optimization of heterogeneous Processing-in-Memory systems—chips with different types of cores built in—connected by on-chip networks, using prior architectural knowledge to guide a multi-stage search and custom layout optimization to explore configurations.
contributions: Joint simulation and search framework extending beyond homogeneous NoC architectures to support heterogeneous PIM cores
Accurate latency modeling via NoC transmission delays and pipeline co-simulation
Three-stage heterogeneous search with priori-knowledge guidance and customized simulated annealing
Customized layout algorithm to minimize communication latency and area; achieves 2.12-2.96x search time reduction
limitations: Abstract does not discuss scalability to very large NoCs, memory overhead of simulation, or comparison with manual expert designs.
primary_theme: Heterogeneous PIM-NoC design space explorer with co-simulation
